clue.text: It may be played on the lawn

definitions.text: It may be played on the lawn

parts.words: It may be played on the lawn
parts.note: suggests a game or music on the grass, but a garden hose is 'played' over a lawn like a jet of water

explanation.surface: A garden game or a lawn concert, something played out on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' tempts toward croquet or a band; in the gardening sense you play a jet of water over something.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener directs, or plays, a flexible water tube over the grass to water it.

clue.text: Top style musical party

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical
a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A stylish production of a musical, with a party afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' means the top of the head, not 'best'.
explanation.definitionFit: A styled arrangement of the hair on top of one's head is a coiffure.

clue.text: Bird lives in hide

indicators.note: the word lives is placed in the middle of the word for hide

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
lives as in 'exists' gives IS

explanation.surface: A bird living in a birdwatchers' hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like the birdwatching shelter, but it is an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: This small yellow-green finch is a songbird of conifer woods.

clue.text: Remain by ascetic

parts.note: per means 'by', as in per post
an ascetic life is austere and severe

explanation.surface: Staying close to a self-denying hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going and carry on without giving up is to remain steadfast at a task.

clue.text: Financial controller's holdings

parts.note: reads like a finance officer's assets, but means the cords that hold a money bag shut, the idiom for control of spending

explanation.surface: The investments owned by a company's finance director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holdings' suggests shares; the cords literally hold a purse closed, and whoever holds them controls the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever has the cords of the money bag decides spending, an idiom for financial control.

clue.text: Office workers go to a Scottish island

parts.note: the employees of an office are its staff

explanation.surface: Office employees head off to a Hebridean island, perhaps on a works outing.
explanation.walkthrough: This small Hebridean island is famous for Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: This small uninhabited island in the Inner Hebrides, off Mull, holds Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: The thanks one gets from a Greek character

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: The gratitude you might receive from someone Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and 'character' means a letter.

clue.text: VAT files go astray? Time for celebration!

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: If your tax records get lost, that is cause for celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the British value added tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala or fete is a period set aside for celebrating.

clue.text: Drink? Ben has it as a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of Ben has it are mixed together

explanation.surface: Ben orders a drink, mixed into a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: The green anise-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: They help those wishing to take cover

definitions.text: They help those wishing to take cover

parts.words: They help those wishing to take cover
parts.note: sounds like people offering shelter, but 'cover' is insurance protection

explanation.surface: Helpers guiding people who want to shelter from danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take cover' suggests ducking for shelter; in finance, cover is a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwriting companies sell policies, which give customers protection called cover.

clue.text: Stops some injustice as essentially unfair

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run within them

explanation.surface: A protest that an injustice ends because it is basically unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run of letters from injusti-CE AS ES-sentially.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or come to an end is synonymous with discontinuing.

clue.text: Being opposed to building seats for spectators?

definitions.meaning: resisting or taking a firm position against something
literally constructing a grandstand for the crowd

explanation.surface: Objecting to a plan to put up stadium seating.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for resisting firmly also literally describes constructing a grandstand.

clue.text: Approach shown by a forceful person

definitions.meaning: the private road leading up to a house
energy and determination, as displayed by a dynamic go-getter

explanation.surface: A method of tackling things that comes from a pushy character.
explanation.definitionFit: A road up to a house is its approach, and ambition and energy is what a forceful person shows.

clue.text: Issue half of them before a race

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the rest
take just the back two of the four letters of them

parts.note: a people or race is a nation

explanation.surface: Half of a team issues something just before a race starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that flows or proceeds out from a source is an outpouring or issue.

clue.text: Threaten with acid? It may result in inevitable fatality

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder rearranged produce, or result in, a new phrase

explanation.surface: An acid attack threat could prove lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may result in' turns the letters of THREATEN and ACID into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fate that is sure to kill is death that cannot be avoided.

clue.text: The longest chords in non-musical circles?

definitions.text: The longest chords in non-musical circles?

parts.words: The longest chords in non-musical circles?
parts.note: chords suggest music, but in geometry a chord is a line across a circle, and the longest passes through the centre

explanation.surface: Musicians' sustained chords, heard in groups that are not musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-musical' tells you the circles are geometric and the chords are lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A line through the centre of a circle is the longest possible chord in geometry.

clue.text: Though he's not there, he's proverbially conspicuous!

definitions.text: Though he's not there, he's proverbially conspicuous!

parts.words: Though he's not there, he's proverbially conspicuous!
parts.note: plays on the proverb 'conspicuous by his absence'

explanation.surface: A paradox about someone noticed precisely because they are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is missing is, by the proverb, conspicuous by his absence.

clue.text: Good people to have around, say, with speech defects

indicators.note: the first piece goes around, enclosing, the second

parts.note: STS is the abbreviation for saints, good people
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: Kind people are good to keep around those with speech problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated hesitations on initial sounds are a form of speech impediment.

clue.text: Gatecrasher?

parts.note: an uninvited party guest, or literally something that crashes through gates

explanation.surface: An uninvited party guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, it smashes city gates, like a siege weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy beam used in sieges to break down doors and gates literally crashes gates.

clue.text: It's useless turning it into a form of fuel

indicators.note: turning the letters around reorders them
a form of a word is a reshaped version of its letters

explanation.surface: Converting something into fuel would be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' and 'a form of' rearrange the letters of IT and FUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointless, achieving nothing, is in vain.

clue.text: Yet they may be quite young trees!

definitions.text: Yet they may be quite young
definitions.meaning: senior people, which paradoxically may be young trees
flowering shrubs or small trees of the genus Sambucus

explanation.surface: A paradox: some old ones may still be saplings.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniors of a community are its older members, and the same word names the Sambucus tree.

clue.text: Greatness, unfortunately, makes enemies

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement is a bad one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadly, being great alienates others.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone, turning a friend hostile, makes an enemy of them.

clue.text: Goodbye for new aide to union leader

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearrangement
a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Farewell to a newly appointed aide to the trade union leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived farewell is used in English to say farewell.

clue.text: Peer in uniform

definitions.meaning: a person of the same rank or standing
the same throughout, even and identical

explanation.surface: A lord dressed in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is one of the same rank, and uniform means the same throughout.

clue.text: Revising his set subject

indicators.note: revising text alters it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student revising for an exam on a set topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition or dissertation topic is the subject one argues.

clue.text: Serving men and women operate from behind it

definitions.text: Serving men and women operate from behind it

parts.words: Serving men and women operate from behind it
parts.note: sounds like military personnel, but these are tennis players serving from behind the court's back line

explanation.surface: Members of the armed forces working from behind the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' suggests the forces; it is tennis serving.
explanation.definitionFit: The back line of a tennis court is where players stand to serve.

clue.text: Relax and pause going round about the Orient

parts.note: the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

indicators.note: letters going round about are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking a rest by touring around the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round about' rearranges PAUSE plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken off or reduce effort is a phrasal verb for relaxing.

clue.text: Greek hero who had an epic journey to get home

definitions.text: Greek hero who had an epic journey to get home

parts.words: Greek hero who had an epic journey to get home
parts.note: the hero of Homer's Odyssey, who took ten years to return to Ithaca after Troy

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek with a long trek back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'epic' is literal: Homer's Odyssey is an epic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's hero, king of Ithaca, spent ten years voyaging home from Troy.
